sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Abhinaya' in Indian classical dance and explain its primary purpose in a performance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Abhinaya refers to the art of expression. Its primary purpose is to communicate emotions, narrate stories, and connect deeply with the audience using facial expressions and body language.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a traditional stage play and a multimedia theatrical performance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A traditional play relies mostly on live acting and spoken dialogue, while a multimedia performance integrates digital elements like projected videos, electronic soundscapes, and advanced lighting effects.

questions.question_text: Explain how physical space and stage blocking affect a theatre scene's impact. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Stage blocking organizes how actors move and position themselves. Good blocking utilizes physical space to show character relationships, direct audience focus, and create visually striking dramatic tension.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe how a puppeteer controls a traditional string puppet (marionette) during a show. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A puppeteer controls a marionette from above using a wooden control bar attached to strings. Moving the bar or pulling specific strings manipulates the puppet's head, arms, and legs.

questions.question_text: Why is 'The Grand Finale' considered a crucial element of any performing arts showcase? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The grand finale brings all performers together for a powerful, high-energy closing sequence. It resolves the narrative tension and leaves a lasting, memorable impression on the audience.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Design a stage backdrop for a play set in a 'Haunted Forest.' Use pencil shading to create depth and eerie textures. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Focus on creating twisted, barren tree silhouettes against a textured, moonlit sky. Marks are awarded for using varying pencil grades to create deep shadows and atmospheric depth, ensuring the foreground elements appear darker and sharper than the foggy background.

questions.question_text: Draw three distinct facial expressions (Joy, Anger, and Surprise) as used in theatrical makeup studies, focusing on eyebrow and mouth positions. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Accurate anatomical distortion for each emotion is required. Joy needs raised cheeks and curved eyes; Anger demands lowered, furrowed brows and tense lips; Surprise requires high eyebrows and a dropped jaw. Marks evaluate clear differentiation and proportional facial feature alignment.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Create an advertisement poster for a school play titled 'The Magic Puppet.' Incorporate bold typography and a central character illustration using bright color pencils. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The poster must have a clear visual hierarchy with the title 'The Magic Puppet' dominating the space. The central puppet figure should be colorful and dynamic. Grading focuses on lettering legibility, harmonious color schemes, and the inclusion of imaginary show details (time/venue) neatly integrated into the layout.

questions.question_text: Design a costume concept sketch for a lead dancer performing a traditional harvest festival dance. Label the different fabrics, accessories, and colors used. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The sketch must reflect cultural authenticity suited for a harvest theme, using flowing lines to suggest movement. Students must provide clear, legible labels pointing to specific garments (e.g., ghagra, turban), jewelry, and props. High marks are given for vibrant color choices and detailed, practical costume design.
